Details

Days are days of beam per µA to reach 3σ at the ATOMKI strength (R = 5.8 × 10⁻⁶, statistics only, Asimov fit in θ × |y| × n_down), MX17 with the big plastics, E_p = 1.10 MeV. Time scales as 1/current.

"Material per lepton" is the median x/X₀ crossed by an X17 lepton on its way to the arms, from one ray-trace applied to every design in the same way (opt_sketch.py). It ranks the designs; it is not Geant4.

Flat target in a chamber

one 200 µm Cu wall, square on (1.4 %)

+ for

  • best measured reach of everything simulated
  • the target is not the vacuum wall: a crack does not vent the line
  • film and stack fully characterised (thermal model, L9)

3

Details

Geant4 run L9 (li20_mo8_dia50), big plastics, 1.10 MeV. The film is perpendicular to the beam inside a CFRP chamber (0.4 mm, r 25 mm). This is "our perpendicular design".

On 24 Oct Pierfrancesco proposed making the target the end of the beam pipe, with no chamber. The diamond window is this same stack turned into that end wall. Sources: TARGET_OPTIONS §7, §14–16; SHAPES_GEANT.md §0.

Diamond window, 45°

one 200 µm Cu wall, square on (1.4 %)

+ for

  • no chamber: the window is the end of the vacuum
  • safe at 1 bar (Ø20, 200–300 µm diamond)
  • tilting moves the rings out of the 90° plane; spreads the spot ×√2

− against

  • the 0.5 mm Al end piece is grazed by legs at 90–140° (σ68 9.1° vs 6.2° without it)
  • Mo K x-rays (17.5 keV) through the diamond: 16 % MM occupancy per arm per µA (est.)
  • window = beam stop = vacuum wall: blistering or a crack vents the line (fast valve)

5

Details

Geant4 diagnostic runs (X17 only, big plastics), SHAPES_GEANT.md §4.1: "no end piece" gives σ68 6.2° (acceptance 0.154). Read off the σ68 → days relation of the full runs, that is ≈ 0.21 d/µA. The bare window (no rings, no line) gives 5.7°. The days are an estimate until a full run with a real adapter.

The trace has no adapter at all, so legs going upstream (90–135°) cross nothing and their bars are at the floor. A real adapter wall will add something there; how much depends on its shape.

Cu ogive

one 200 µm Cu wall, square on (1.4 %)

+ for

  • steep walls everywhere: 90° legs cross ≈ 1.1× the wall, not 10×
  • no flange in the arms’ view (base 63 mm back)

− against

  • still ≥ 1.4 % X₀ of Cu on every lepton (median 2.9 %)

  • the trace under-reads Cu shells (hemisphere: 12.6° traced, 22° in Geant4)

Be ogive

one 200 µm Cu wall, square on (1.4 %)

+ for

  • ×8 less material per lepton than in Cu, half the window
  • no chamber, no tube in view
  • keeps the shell idea Pierfrancesco prefers

− against

  • a custom part from a Be shop: ~5–25 k€ each, months (ESTIMATE, ask for a quote)
  • needs LNL safety approval (EU carcinogen); brittle, so a failure leaves Be fragments in the line
  • the same 441 keV issue on the flank as the Cu ogive, unless the Li is masked to the tip

9

Details

Ray-trace only (opt_shell_material.py, liner included). Material check (TARGET_OPTIONS §20, ESTIMATE): at 1 bar the 300 µm Be shell has ×20 margin on buckling and on stress (200 µm: ×7); the tip runs 41 K above the air at 4 µA with a fan; join it by a thick Be collar at the base, bonded by the vendor into a Ti/SS CF ring (or an O-ring or glue), 63 mm behind the tip and out of the arms’ view. The cheap alternative is Al 6061-T6 at 0.3–0.4 mm + Mo (σ68 7.4–7.9° traced, about the window; 0.2 mm Al buckles at 1.8 bar).

Common to every design (not in the costs): Li evaporation at LNL; a fast-closing valve upstream (~5–10 k€ if LNL has none), because in every design the target or its chamber is the vacuum wall; 2–3 spare targets per campaign.

10

Details

Margin = failure pressure (buckling, with a knockdown: 0.56 for tubes and cones, 0.2 for spheres) or strength (yield; CVD diamond 280 MPa, the growth side in tension) over the 1 bar load. CERN practice asks ≥ 3 for buckling. "Simulated" is the geometry Geant4 ran; "to build" is the change recommended here. Li rise: the full heat path to the air at 4 µA (4.4 W at 1.10 MeV) with a fan (h = 100 W/m²/K); the Li must stay below ~150 °C. The 20 µm Li runs at 0.12–0.5 µA, ×8–30 less heat. Costs are first-unit ranges from public prices and quotes, not quotes (TARGET_OPTIONS §21; opt_practical.py).

Physics against practicality: the cheap, routine designs are also the fast ones

Each dot is a design (its colour as on the other slides); the bar is the cost range, coloured by difficulty (green routine, gold development, red specialist + approval). Lower-left is best.

difficulty 1–2

11

Details

Days per µA from the Geant4 runs of the deck (big plastics, 1.10 MeV). The Be variants buy little reach for ×3–10 the cost and a safety approval, so take them only if the cheaper version of the same idea is not enough. ESTIMATE costs (TARGET_OPTIONS §21).

Three of the simulated geometries must change before they are built

Closed-form shell, plate and fin estimates; the LNL mechanical office should confirm by FEA

Flat target: the CFRP chamber

0.4 mm × 600 mm, as in L9, buckles at 0.35 bar. Make it ≥ 1 mm and ≤ 300 mm long (×7). Cost to the leptons (trace): σ68 7.4° → 8.2°.

Windows: the diamond

200 µm over Ø20 carries 198 MPa at its clamped edge: margin ×1.4 on the weak (growth) side. 300 µm: 85 MPa, ×3.3. Geant4 L10: 0.28 against 0.27 d/µA. Order 300 µm.

Ogives: the wall

Al 200 µm buckles at 1.8 bar; 300 µm at 4.9. Be: 7 → 20 bar. His Cu 200 µm: 3.0 bar, just under CERN's ×3.

Heat is not the limit anywhere

≤ 70 K at 4 µA in every design. In the window it is the Ti rings and the 55 mm end piece that carry it (diamond 2 K, Ti rings 17 K, joint 2 K, end piece 25 K), not the diamond: braze or glue makes no difference.

Targets are consumables

Where the beam stops, H builds up: Cu blisters after ~5 days at 1 µA, Ta/Mo after ≥ 16 (§5); diamond is untested. At the 0.12–0.5 µA the 20 µm Li needs, plan 2–3 spares per campaign.

The real gates

Be (end piece, hemisphere, ogive): LNL safety approval and a Be-shop quote, 3–6 months. Everything else is the LNL workshop plus one CVD-diamond vendor (8–14 weeks).

Decisions and what this does not settle

Decide

Build the 45° window on a wide, short adapter: ≈ 0.21 d/µA, no chamber, safe at 1 bar.

If Pierfrancesco keeps the shell: Al 0.3–0.4 mm + Mo first, Be 0.3 mm + Mo as the upgrade (cost, safety), never Cu (2.4 d/µA in Geant4 for the Cu hemisphere).

Perpendicular only in a chamber (0.22); as a window, tilt it (0° costs ×1.36).

Not settled

The adapter and both ogives need Geant4 runs. Their numbers here are a diagnostic and a trace.

The ogive’s flank sees 2.4× the Li, so the 441 keV resonance enters. Spot size and Li on the flank are unknown.

Window: Mo K x-rays in the MM, and H blistering of the Mo stop. Both need a bench test.

Reach is statistics only, at R(ATOMKI); no systematics.
